title: VC-7 residual: live detached exit/reattach acceptance receipt (launch on the local detached profile, exit Pi while an exactly-once effect marker proves execution continued, relaunch and reattach by invocation ref as zero-control observer, post-host-loss inspection reports unknown with reconciliation guidance); measurement-only, src untouched
description: Gap (measured at rig HEAD, branch workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md section "Implementation status at 2026-10-15" records "VC-7 has a same-machine private detached process profile" and that it "remains open for its broader native/live release acceptance". VC-7 children cover fault-injection conformance (wb-0kg.1) and executable identity (wb-0kg.2); the operator journey itself (Pi exits without stopping execution, then reattach) has no bead. Scope (measurement-only, src untouched, no hot files): qa/workbench/detached-reattach-receipt.mjs (new) launches a saved workflow on the local detached profile, exits the Pi client process entirely, proves continued execution via an exactly-once effect marker written after client exit, relaunches and reattaches by invocation ref as a zero-control observer, then kills the host and asserts post-loss inspection reports unknown with producer reconciliation guidance; test/workbench-detached-receipt.test.ts (new) is the red-first assessor over the receipt shape. Exit 2 for honest environment unavailability. Same-machine OS discretionary access only; makes no remote-authentication or crash-durability claim.
acceptance_criteria: QUOTES: docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md#vertical-cuts (VC-7) requires "Pi exits without stopping execution." -- journey proves it with an exactly-once effect marker written AFTER full Pi client exit, then a reattach by invocation ref. docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md#optional-local-detached-profile: "Closing or exiting Pi disconnects the client, not the execution host. Inspection after host loss reports unknown with producer reconciliation guidance; it does not replay a saved terminal verdict or rerun JavaScript." -- falsifier kills the host and asserts the post-loss inspection reports unknown with guidance, never a replayed verdict and never a rerun. Also per the same section the profile "is same-machine OS discretionary-access control only, not remote authentication": the receipt must label itself accordingly and claim nothing more. Receipt carries revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output per docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md#truth-labels-and-release-gates; exit 2 on honest unavailability.
